chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Ibn Miskan, from Zurara, who said:

He said to me: 'Do you know why the cubit and the two cubits have been established?' I said: 'Why?' He said: 'For the place of the obligatory [prayer], it is for you that you may pray optional [prayers] from the decline of the sun until the shadow reaches one cubit. So when it reaches one cubit, begin with the obligatory [prayer] and leave the optional [prayers].'

key_terms.الذِّرَاعُ: cubit (a unit of measurement based on the forearm)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the shadow length in determining the time for obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential wisdom behind the shadow measurements (dhira') that demarcate the transition from the Dhuhr to the Asr prayer times. It establishes a clear hierarchy where the period between solar noon (Zawal) and the shadow reaching one cubit is reserved for voluntary (nafl) prayers, which must be concluded before the obligatory Asr prayer begins. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining distinct temporal boundaries for ritual obligations to ensure proper devotion and order in worship.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Fazalat in Ayoub, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara who said,

‘Heasws said to me: ‘Do you know why a cubit and two cubits have been made to be?’ I said, ‘Why?’ Heasws said: ‘In place of the Obligatory (Salāt). It is for you that you can pray Optional (Salāts) from the (start of the) decline of the sun up it (the shadow) reaching one cubit. So when it reaches to one cubit, begin with the Obligatory and leave the Optional’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ariy has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from ibn Muskan from Zurarah who has said the following:

“He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘Do you know why one and two yards are set?’ I (the narrator) said, ‘Why are they set?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because of obligatory Salah (prayer). You can perform optional Salah (prayer) soon after the sun declines (to the west at noontime) until it become one yard, but if you begin the obligatory one, you do not perform optional Salah (prayer).”’
